takeaway: ADH comes from the supraoptic nucleus and rises with low pressure or high osmolality; high arterial pressure does not stimulate it.

question.text: Which statement regarding the regulation of sodium and water reabsorption is incorrect?

answer.text: ADH secretion is stimulated by an increased arterial pressure.
answer.say: Antidiuretic hormone secretion is stimulated by an increased arterial pressure.

lines.text: Antidiuretic hormone is made in the supraoptic nucleus of the hypothalamus, so that statement is correct.
It is stimulated by raised osmolality, a fall in circulating volume, or reduced arterial pressure.
lines.say: It is stimulated by raised osmolality, a fall in circulating volume, or reduced arterial pressure.

lines.text: Aldosterone stimulates sodium reabsorption in the distal tubule, also correct.
Renin is released from the juxtaglomerular cells when sodium or afferent arteriole pressure falls, correct again.
But high arterial pressure does not raise antidiuretic hormone; it lowers it.
Low pressure means more of it, so the incorrect statement is the last one.
